editorial:
Imagine living in a huge house with plenty of money and a perfect image, only to have it all fall apart in one summer. You get to follow a wealthy British Indian family who seems to have everything together until a death in the family brings everyone back home. Once they are all under one roof, the polite smiles fade and the real fighting begins. It feels like a slow burn where you can tell something bad is about to happen, and the tension between the siblings and parents makes you feel like you are right there in the room with them during their biggest arguments.

The acting is the best part here because the actors make the family drama feel very real and painful. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the shock of the secrets coming out makes it worth the wait. You should definitely check this out if you love movies about messy families and hidden lies.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the final big secret is revealed about the family patriarch. You find out that the wealth was built on lies and betrayal that hurt the people closest to him. The family has to decide if they can actually forgive each other or if the damage is too deep. In the end, they don't get a perfect happy ending, but they finally stop lying, which lets them start healing.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family dramas and uncovering secrets.
